bill_popover.outside_desc: Cash, or someone paid for me. No amount enters the numbers.
bill_popover.pick_transaction: Or point at the transaction that paid it (optional)
bill_popover.no_candidates: No transaction matches this rule's snippets.

day_details.empty_select: Click any day on the calendar to see that day's transactions.
day_details.mark_due: Set a bill due on day {day}

about.tagline: The money is yours. So is the data.
about.promise: No account, no cloud, no internet. Everything you record stays on your computer, and only you see it.
about.disclaimer: This app helps you organize your personal finances. It doesn't give investment advice or work as a bank.

specs.label: No catch
specs.value: You can see everything it does

tx_table.empty_desc: Import your bank's .ofx statement and transactions show up here, already categorized by your rules.

categories.name: Name
categories.empty_desc: Categories group your spending in the dashboard and reports. Create the first one in the form above.

rules.reach_title: Transactions whose description matches any snippet of this rule — including ones you categorized by hand or that a higher-priority rule claimed.
rules.reach_none: No transaction matches this rule. The snippet might be worded differently than in the statement.
rules.empty: A rule says "if the description contains X, use category Y" — and it applies on its own to every import from then on. E.g.: "uber" → Transport.

rule_form.pattern_placeholder_more: another way the bank describes it
rule_form.due_day_title: Day of the month the bill is due. Leave empty if the rule has no fixed due date.
rule_form.pay_lead_same: In the month it falls due
rule_form.due_day_invalid: Due day must be between 1 and 31 (or empty).

rule_due_picker.title: Due on day {day}
rule_due_picker.desc: The bill you pick falls due on day {day} every month, not just this one.
rule_due_picker.desc_any: Pick the day of the month, and the bill that falls due on it every month.

dashboard.no_data_12m: No data in the last 12 months
dashboard.caption_tx_one: one tx in the period (excl. transfers)
dashboard.investments_note: tracked separately · doesn't count as expense or income
dashboard.invested_balance_title: Contributed this month − redeemed this month. Positive: net investment. Negative: net withdrawal from investments.

import.dropzone_desc_1: Export your bank's monthly statement (Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, etc.) in the
import.dropzone_desc_2: format and drop it here — or click to choose a file.
import.reversal_reversal: This transaction is a reversal — it undoes another one. Added together they net to zero. Unchecked by default so it doesn't inflate expenses/income.
import.reversal_reversed: This transaction was reversed (undone by the bank). Added together with the reversal it nets to zero. Unchecked by default.
import.reversal_refund: This transaction is a refund — money returned from a transfer you sent. Added together they net to zero. Unchecked by default.
import.reversal_refunded: This transaction was refunded. Added together with the refund it nets to zero. Unchecked by default.
import.reversal_legend_one: {n} reversal/refund pair ↔ original detected — unchecked by default because the sum is zero (not real spending or income). Check it manually if you want to import it anyway.
import.reversal_legend_many: {n} reversal/refund pairs ↔ original detected — unchecked by default because the sum is zero (not real spending or income). Check them manually if you want to import them anyway.
import.classified_one: categorized automatically via existing rules + new company match.
import.classified_many: categorized automatically via existing rules + new company matches.
import.rules_created_hint: Deleting a rule undoes the categorization of the transactions it matched.
import.rule_category_title: Category suggested by the lookup — you can change it
import.unresolved_hint: The lookup service returned data, but its business activity isn't mapped to a category. Choose one manually.
import.choose_category_first: Choose a category before creating the rule.
import.delete_rule_confirm: Delete rule "{pattern}"? Transactions categorized by it will become uncategorized.
import.neutralized_pairs_title: Reversal/refund ↔ reversed transaction pairs (unchecked by default)

tx_notes.create_rule_cta: Create a rule from this transaction
tx_notes.pattern_title: Snippet that will be searched for within each transaction's description

tx_search.title: Which transaction paid this bill?
tx_search.desc: {bill} · due in {month}. The search looks at every transaction, not only the ones the rule matches.
tx_search.empty_desc: Try another term, or settle the bill outside the statement.

kind_guide.title: What does each type mean?
kind_guide.transfer: Money moving around: card bill, between your own accounts, investments. Excluded from income, expenses, and balance.

category_panel.title: Edit category
category_panel.kind_hint: Only "Transfer" changes the calculations: it's excluded from income, expenses, and balance.
category_panel.color_hint: The color identifies the category in the dashboard and charts.
category_panel.scope_note: Renaming or changing the color takes effect immediately on every transaction in this category.

categories_page.desc: Create, edit, or delete any category. The 13 starter categories come pre-created but can be freely modified or removed — deleting one leaves its transactions uncategorized and deletes its rules.
categories_page.delete_confirm: Delete "{name}"? Its rules are deleted too.
categories_page.delete_confirm_one: Delete "{name}"? {n} transaction will become uncategorized, and its rules are deleted too.
categories_page.delete_confirm_many: Delete "{name}"? {n} transactions will become uncategorized, and its rules are deleted too.

rule_panel.title: Edit rule
rule_panel.if_contains_any: If the description contains any of these
rule_panel.patterns_hint: The rule applies when ANY of these appear in the description. Use short, stable snippets — pasting the whole statement line breaks if the bank changes a number.
rule_panel.due_day_hint: Day of the month the bill is due — this is what places the rule on the calendar. Empty = no fixed due date.
rule_panel.priority_hint: When two rules match the same transaction, the higher-priority one wins.
rule_panel.scope_note: Editing the rule doesn't touch what's already categorized. Use "Apply to existing" to reprocess uncategorized transactions.

rule_matches.title: Rule transactions
rule_matches.empty_desc: No description in your statement contains this rule's snippets. Check whether they're worded the way your bank writes them.
rule_matches.note: Matches any snippet in the rule, regardless of the category the transaction is currently in.

rule_apply.title: Review changes
rule_apply.subtitle_one: 1 transaction changes category if you apply the rules.
rule_apply.subtitle_many: {n} transactions change category if you apply the rules.
rule_apply.group_override_note: Applying the rule replaces the current category. The app doesn't track who set it — it could've been you or a rule that has since changed. That's why none come pre-checked.
rule_apply.nothing_to_do: The rules are already applied — no transaction would change category.

rules_page.desc: Rules like "if description contains X, category Y" are applied automatically on every import. Manual categorization is never overwritten.

calendar_page.subtitle: Real inflows and outflows for the month, day by day (transfers and investments excluded). Click a day to see everything that happened.

onboarding.title: Your finances, on your Mac.
onboarding.subtitle: No cloud, no login, no subscription. Drag your bank's OFX statement in and Finoinc organizes everything into a local SQLite file.
onboarding.language_desc: This decides the categories and rules Finoinc starts you with. You can change it later in Settings.

suggestions.title: Rule suggestions
suggestions.desc: that recur without a tax ID (card debit, person-to-person transfers, bills). Inflows don't appear here — income is tracked by counterparty in the Dashboard (Income Sources).
suggestions.empty: Nothing here — every recurring counterparty already has a category, or raise the occurrence filter.
suggestions.subtitle: Recurring expenses that don't have a category yet — card debit, person-to-person transfers, bills. Inflows live in the Dashboard, under Income Sources.

settings.title: Settings
settings.language_desc: Choose the interface language. The native macOS menu changes the next time the app starts.
settings.database_desc: All your transactions live in this file on your Mac. Nothing is sent to the cloud.
settings.backup_desc: Exports a copy of the file to any folder. Restoring REPLACES the current database — back up first.
settings.restore_confirm: This will REPLACE your current database. You'll need to restart the app afterward. Continue?
settings.restore_done_msg: Backup restored. Quit and reopen Finoinc (Cmd+Q, then reopen) to see the restored transactions.
settings.about_line: 100% local personal finances on your Mac.
settings.enrich_desc: During import, queries an external service to identify the company behind each {taxId} in the description and suggest a category. Requires internet.
settings.freshness_desc: Shows on the dashboard how far your data goes and how many days are missing since the newest imported transaction.

watch.pitch_title: Download the statement on your phone. Your Mac finds it on its own.
watch.pitch_body: Save the .ofx file to a folder on your Mac — via iCloud, AirDrop, or a direct download. Finoinc notices when a new statement shows up and opens the review right away.
watch.privacy_note: The app only reads .ofx files, and only in the folders you choose. Nothing leaves your Mac.
watch.create_icloud_confirm: The "Finoinc" folder doesn't exist in your iCloud Drive yet. Create it now?
watch.folder_missing: folder not found — it may have been moved or removed
watch.hint_dropzone: Tired of dragging files? Let Finoinc find the statement on its own — setup takes 10s
watch.error_duplicate: That folder is already in the watched list.
watch.error_unreachable: Couldn't access that folder — it may have been moved, renamed, or is on an unmounted volume.
watch.error_remove: Couldn't remove that folder from the list.
watch.error_create_icloud: Couldn't create the folder in iCloud Drive.
watch.error_reveal: Couldn't open that folder in Finder.
watch.error_scan: Couldn't scan the folders right now.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.subtitle: Let an AI agent on this Mac read — and, if you allow it, change — your finances.
mcp.connection_desc: Turns on a server on this Mac. Nothing is published to the internet.
mcp.only_while_open: Answers only while Finoinc is open.
mcp.url_label: Paste this URL into your agent
mcp.tools_write_desc: The agent changes your data. Every one starts off.
mcp.tool_list_transactions_desc: Lists bank transactions, newest first. Filters by month, category, a text fragment of the description, or only the ones with no category yet.
mcp.tool_get_month_summary_desc: Everything about one month in a single answer: income, expense and balance, spending per category, who paid the money in, and how much went to investments.
mcp.tool_get_trend_desc: Income and expense month by month, to see whether spending is rising or falling.
mcp.tool_list_bills_desc: Recurring bills for a month, each with its due day and whether it is already paid, still due, or overdue.
mcp.tool_list_categories_desc: Every category, with the id needed to categorize a transaction.
mcp.tool_categorize_transactions_desc: Assigns a category to one or more transactions.
mcp.tool_create_rule_desc: Creates a rule that categorizes any transaction whose description contains one of the given fragments.
mcp.tool_settle_bill_desc: Marks a bill occurrence as settled for a month.
mcp.window_desc: How far back the agent can reach — for reading and for changing.
mcp.window_cutoff_none: The agent sees your whole history.
mcp.activity_desc: The last {n} calls. Kept in memory only — gone when you quit.
mcp.activity_empty_desc: What your agent asks for shows up here.
